brief: UBS reports the Fed unanimously raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike in three years, with 16 of 18 participants projecting a further increase this year and the 10-year Treasury yield hitting 5.02%, its highest since 2007. The S&P 500 fell only modestly, which UBS reads as investors staying focused on resilient growth and earnings, so UBS's base case is a shallower cycle than markets price (markets price three more hikes by 2027; UBS expects one more 25bp hike in December), forecasting S&P 500 earnings up 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027 and a price target of 8,400 by June 2027. The ECB has already hiked, the BoJ raised to 1.25% (highest since 1995), and the BoE held at 3.75% but signaled more tightening ahead; UBS thinks markets are pricing longer tightening cycles than will be delivered and rates fixed income Attractive. Separately, Middle East supply disruption (Strait of Hormuz, a damaged Saudi pipeline) has kept Brent near USD 100-102; UBS's base case assumes limited escalation and it recently raised its Brent forecast to USD 95 at year-end and USD 90 in March 2027, recommending diversified commodity exposure.
